primitives.name: Strong Aggregating Algorithm
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - The **Strong Aggregating Algorithm (SAA)** adapted to the multiclass Brier game: maintain weights over experts, update multiplicatively with exp(-loss), and compute each round's "generalized prediction" from the weight-weighted expert predictions.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'w_k^t': 'weight of expert k at time t (dimensionless)', 'γ_k^t': 'predicted probability vector of expert k at time t (probability simplex)', 'γ_t': 'aggregated prediction at time t (probability simplex)'}
primitives.assumptions: Experts provide full probability distributions; outcomes observed after prediction; Brier game is mixable with optimal learning rate η = 1.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When expert correlations approach unity or when loss diverges due to extreme misprediction.

layer2.mapping: SAA maps to GSE's ensemble combiner by dynamically reweighting sub-expert models based on Brier loss history, enabling adaptive belief fusion under uncertainty.
layer2.telemetry: Cumulative Brier loss compared against best expert + ln K

primitives.name: Brier Loss Function
primitives.verbatim_quote: Equations & assumptions - Multiclass Brier loss: **λ(ω, γ) = Σ_o (γ{o} - δ_ω{o})2**, where ω is the realized outcome, γ the predicted probability distribution, δ the Kronecker delta.

primitives.assumptions: Outcomes are discrete and mutually exclusive; predictions are proper probability distributions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When predicted probabilities are degenerate or when realized outcome is outside support of γ.

primitives.breakdown_regime: When the number of experts grows without bound or when loss becomes unbounded.

reasoning_traces.think:
The Strong Aggregating Algorithm (SAA) operates within the Brier game framework, where each expert provides a full probability distribution over outcomes. At each time step, SAA maintains a set of weights over these experts, which are updated multiplicatively according to the negative exponential of the Brier loss incurred. This process ensures that experts who make better predictions gain higher influence in future decisions. The resulting generalized prediction is a weighted average of all expert predictions, maintaining consistency with the Brier scoring rule. The regret bound guarantees that the cumulative loss of the learner will not exceed the best expert's cumulative loss by more than ln K, where K is the number of experts. This implies that even in adversarial settings, the algorithm performs nearly as well as the best static expert in hindsight. However, the tightness of this bound depends critically on the independence of experts; correlated experts reduce the effectiveness of the bound. The dual nature of SAA lies in its ability to balance exploration (trying different experts) and exploitation (favoring high-performing ones), making it suitable for dynamic environments such as sports prediction where outcomes are uncertain and evolving.
